# `Q-2-61` — List-table cell span is not empty

> A list-table cell starts with a span that has content and a
> `colspan` or `rowspan` attribute. Only an empty span at the start of
> a cell sets the cell's span.

## What this means

A list-table cell reads its `colspan`, `rowspan`, and `align`
attributes from an *empty* span at the very start of the cell. The
cell's text follows the span:

```markdown
::: {.list-table}
- - []{colspan=2} Merged
- - a
  - b
:::
```

When the span has content, as in `[Merged]{colspan=2}`, it is an
ordinary span inside an ordinary cell. The attribute stays on the span
(HTML output gets `<span colspan="2">`), and the cell does not span two
columns.

## How to fix

Empty the span and put the text after it:

```markdown
- - []{colspan=2} Merged
```
